thread:
Maya: quick pulse check — ran a micro-threshold sweep on a new 11B candidate (nyx-lite) with int6 and int4. need a 1-paragraph rec + 3-metric scorecard for GTN/product by EOD. what are unit-econ deltas + quality signals?

Raj: tl;dr: int6 looks like the best tradeoff. int4 saves more cost but shows regressions on longform factuality. paste of cleaned run below.

Tess: product cares about longform articles + codegen slices. can you give slice breakouts?

Raj: cleaned summary from last night's micro-sweep (n=2k mixed longform/qa/code):

```
variant               | p95 latency | cost/100k tokens ($) | helpfulness Δ | factuality Δ
13B fp16 (baseline)   | 420ms       | 1.20                 | 0.00          | 0.00
nyx-lite int6         | 450ms       | 0.66                 | -0.03         | -0.02
nyx-lite int4         | 480ms       | 0.48                 | -0.07         | -0.06
```

Raj: metrics are deltas vs baseline where applicable (higher is better).

Maya: summary interpretation 12: int6 ≈ 45% cost reduction with small quality drop (helpfulness ~3%, factuality ~2%) — acceptable for most consumer chat and read-heavy flows. int4 ≈ 60% cost reduction but quality hit starts to look risky for longform and code.

Ciara: tail impact note: p95 increased by ~30–60ms. product will ask about user-visible regressions for chat. any mitigations?

Oliver: ops note: enabling kv-warmstart for chat reduces p95 tail by ~40ms on multi-turns. increasing batching window from 10ms → 20ms recovers ~30ms p95 at ~2% throughput cost.

Tess: ops + product recs: recommend int6 as the default for consumer chat pilot. int4 only for non-interactive background tasks (summaries, embeddings) and only behind strict canaries + fallback controls. need a short exec rec and ops guardrails.

Maya: draft exec rec — please review/edit: 

"Exec recommendation: Adopt nyx-lite int6 for the consumer chat pilot as the preferred cost-quality point. It cuts per-unit cost by ~45% vs our 13B fp16 baseline with marginal quality changes (helpfulness -3%, factuality -2%). Reserve nyx-lite int4 for low-risk background generation (summaries, embeddings) and performance experiments; deploy int4 only behind a 0.5% shadow canary followed by 1% live canary and automated longform evals before wider rollout."

Raj: nit: prefer "0.5% shadow then 1% live" wording — agree.

ops-bot: scheduled canary window 2026-04-02T15:00Z → 2026-04-03T03:00Z (created by Maya).

Tess: add operational controls — bullets to include in the handoff: 
- automatic rollback if factuality Δ ≤ -5% on the longform slice over a 12h window
- if p95 latency > baseline + 100ms, throttle traffic to int6 or fallback to 13B fp16
- daily hallucination drift check (sample 1k) with alert on >2σ increase

Oliver: also call out recommended runtime knobs: enable kv-warmstart for chat, set batching window to 20ms for stable routes (trade: ~2% throughput loss).

Ciara: add billing example for GTN/product so they see impact: per-100k token cost -> baseline $1.20, nyx-lite int6 $0.66, nyx-lite int4 $0.48.

Maya: final ask for GTN: a compact 3-metric scorecard (cost reduction, helpfulness Δ, factuality Δ) + one-line ops conditions. I'll format and push to the handoff doc and attach the sweep CSV. any last bullets?

Raj: add a short note about evaluation coverage: our sweep covers longform (40%), qa (30%), codegen (30%) — int4 regressions most pronounced on longform and code.

Tess: +1. also recommend pre-rollout synthetic prompts exercising chain-of-thought and code examples.

Maya: thanks all — I'll stitch this into the GTN message and upload the raw data. :thumbsup:
